heading: January 2025 finalization dispute
body:
On January 15, 2025, the United States and Qatar — the brokers of the agreement — proclaimed that a deal had been reached with Hamas to end the 15-month war in Gaza triggered by the October 7, 2023 onslaught.[n] Israel nonetheless held off through Thursday, January 16 from officially declaring the ceasefire-hostage release deal concluded, insisting details remained to be finalized and that Hamas was throwing last-minute wrenches into the negotiations.[n] Mossad chief [[david-barnea|David Barnea]], head of Israel's negotiating team, remained in Doha as of that afternoon, having been dispatched to the Qatari capital the previous Saturday night.[n] The Prime Minister's Office issued a statement that morning accusing Hamas of backing out of some agreements and creating a "crisis" in finalizing the deal; no evidence was provided and Hamas denied the allegation.[n]

In the early hours of Friday, January 17, Prime Minister [[benjamin-netanyahu|Benjamin Netanyahu]]'s office said on X that the negotiating team had reported "agreements have been reached on a deal for the release of the hostages" in Doha, and that Netanyahu had ordered the security cabinet to convene later that day — a day later than originally intended.[n] It was not immediately clear whether the full cabinet would meet Friday or Saturday, with The Times of Israel reporting, citing a Netanyahu spokesperson, that the full cabinet meeting would not take place until Saturday night, potentially delaying the ceasefire's entry into force until Monday.[n] Netanyahu has been accused of deliberately sabotaging previous deals for his own political benefit.[n]

Badlands contributor GhostofBasedPatrickHenry read the sequence as a trap closing on Netanyahu: because Donald Trump had already spiked the football with repeated Truth Social celebrations, the delay registered publicly as Netanyahu pulling defeat from the jaws of victory, with the first hostage exchange falling on the day of Trump's inauguration.[n] He noted Netanyahu's coalition would retain a Knesset majority even without [[itamar-ben-gvir|Itamar Ben Gvir]]'s party, but would fall to a minority if [[bezalel-smotrich|Bezalel Smotrich]]'s [[religious-zionism-party|Religious Zionism]] also followed through on threats to depart, while opposition parties promised to support the coalition so long as it advanced the deal.[n]

heading: January 2025 hostage deal delay
body: Through January 16, 2025 Netanyahu withheld public comment on the Gaza ceasefire-hostage deal announced by mediators the previous evening, saying he would speak only when terms were finalized, while his office accused Hamas of reneging on key parts of the agreement to extort last-minute concessions — an allegation offered without evidence and denied by Hamas.[n] In the early hours of January 17 his office announced on X that agreements had been reached on a deal for the release of the hostages and that he had ordered the security cabinet to convene later that day, a day later than originally intended.[n] Netanyahu has been accused of deliberately sabotaging previous deals for his own political benefit.[n] Badlands commentary argued that Trump's public framing of the deal as already done left Netanyahu "pinched," with his coalition retaining a Knesset majority without Ben Gvir's party but falling to a minority should Bezalel Smotrich's Religious Zionism also quit.[n]

heading: Doha negotiations (January 2025)
body: As Mossad chief and head of Israel's negotiating team, Barnea was dispatched to Doha on the night of Saturday, January 11, 2025, and remained in the Qatari capital as of the afternoon of Thursday, January 16, according to an official familiar with the talks, while Israel held off on formally declaring that a ceasefire-hostage release deal had been reached with Hamas.[n]

heading: January 2025 ceasefire finalization dispute
body: As mediators announced a phased deal on January 15, 2025 to end the 15-month war in Gaza, Israel's Prime Minister's Office accused Hamas of backing out of some agreements and creating a "crisis" in finalizing the deal, alleging it was throwing last-minute wrenches into negotiations to extort concessions.[n] No evidence was provided for the allegation and Hamas denied it.[n] Agreements on the hostage release were reported concluded in Doha in the early hours of January 17.[n]

heading: Gaza ceasefire and Accords expansion (January 2025)
body: In announcing that he would use the momentum of the Gaza ceasefire to expand the [[abraham-accords|Abraham Accords]], President-elect Donald Trump wrote on Truth Social that his national security team, "through the efforts of Special Envoy to the Middle East, Steve Witkoff," would continue to work closely with Israel and US allies to ensure that Gaza never again becomes a terrorist safe haven.[n]
